html:
The Dayton Agreement ended the Bosnian War. It was negotiated at an air base in Dayton, Ohio, in November 1995 and signed in Paris on 14 December 1995 by the presidents of Bosnia, Serbia and Croatia.

It kept Bosnia and Herzegovina as one state but split it into two entities, a Bosniak and Croat federation and a Serb republic, with a weak central government and a three member presidency. Its annex became Bosnia's constitution. A NATO led force kept the peace, and an international High Representative got broad powers. Dayton stopped the killing but froze the ethnic divisions of the war, and the system it created makes the country hard to govern.
sum: The Dayton Agreement ended the Bosnian War. It was negotiated at an air base in Dayton, Ohio, in November 1995 and signed in Paris on 14 December 1995 by the presidents of Bosnia, Serbia and Croatia.
